component.name: BlueFerry
component.summary: Your iPhone's messages and notifications on the Linux desktop

description.p: BlueFerry brings a paired iPhone to the Linux desktop over standard Bluetooth profiles — no Mac relay, no cloud service, no subscription.
This app is the graphical front-end for the BlueFerry daemon:

ul.li: Read SMS and iMessage conversations and send replies
Control which mirrored iPhone notifications create desktop popups
One iPhone page for connection health, pairing, and maintenance

description.p: Restores Debian backend startup on systemd 255 while retaining stronger service sandboxing in other native packages.
Adds local conversation deletion, improves pairing diagnostics and Bluetooth recovery, and fixes backend startup on systemd 255.
Recovers ANCS when a previously authorized iPhone stops responding after a Bluetooth reconnect.
Recovers iPhone notifications after reconnects, makes message editors expand and wrap, and improves conversation-storage recovery.
Prevents the privileged Bluetooth setup helper from hanging when pairing under systemd.
Improves cross-distro pairing and privileged setup, makes controller capability checks advisory, and polishes Qt startup, connection health, and group messaging.
Adds native Linux packages, compatibility and explicit pairing modes, build-aware daemon restarts, and ANCS recovery after BlueZ restarts.
Lets you pick a Bluetooth controller when more than one is present and keeps pairing, scanning, and forget on that radio.
Improves interactive Bluetooth pairing, diagnostics, and handling when a saved device is forgotten outside BlueFerry.
Adds the Textual terminal client, notification deep links, KDE tray integration, and automatic daemon restarts after package upgrades.
Backend-owned safe thread routing, group replies, Apple-ID contacts, reconnect supervision, privacy controls, and split desktop clients.
First GTK4 / libadwaita desktop app — conversations, a notification feed and a setup/status page.
